novelty_flags: 'An LLM planner adds nothing beyond the world model' is not new (Gupta et al. 2025; Wainrib et al. 2026 for weaker models).
Exact-k compliance failures of LLM planners at batch ~100-128 are documented (BioDiscoveryAgent, Wainrib et al.); our id-format localisation is an engineering finding, not a contribution.
The O'Neil -> ALMANAC transfer evaluation of an in-context combination model already exists (ScreenShot).
World-model over-optimism on selected items is the optimizer's curse (Smith & Winkler 2006); the two-screen measurement is a replication, not a discovery.

Remaining defensible novelty: a randomised in-shortlist audit that certifies FDR / yield claims for any (including LLM) planner, with its measured price; no source found that does exactly this, but the underlying exchangeability argument is standard.
